shorts.description:
Growth hack: word your problems as personal deficiencies.

“My sales people suck” VS 
“I don’t know how to hire train and manage great salespeople.”

If you can improve it, it’s a skill.
If it’s a skill, you can learn it.

But you have to admit you suck before it can get better.
shorts.title: “Why Won’t My Team Work Harder?”

shorts.description:
Affiliates in a nutshell:

1) Figure out who has your audience
2) Figure out what they want more than anything
3) Give it to them, then ask them if they’d be willing to share something that benefits them - and their audience - that happens to help you.
shorts.title: How to Explain What You Do to Anyone

shorts.description:
You can get “good enough” at almost anything in 20 hours of focused effort.

The problem is…most people spend a decade delaying the first hour.
shorts.title: It Takes 20 Hours — But People Wait a Decade to Start

shorts.description:
Bad salespeople keep selling after a prospect says yes. They turn 1 sale into 0.

Good salespeople close and move on.
They turn 0 sale into 1.

Great salespeople close and ask for a referral. They turn 0 sale into 2.

Close first. Then, ask for more.
shorts.title: Ask "Who Else Do You Know?" After Every Sale

shorts.description:
How to lose a sale: get the prospect to disagree with you.

How to never have them disagree: answer their questions with questions about their questions.

The person who gives concrete responses now has to defend them.

And if you’re on defense, you’re not closing.
shorts.title: Don't Answer the Question, Ask a Question About the Question

shorts.description:
The fastest path to $10M is often not the fastest path to $100m.

In this way, patience is strategy.
shorts.title: You're Shooting Yourself in the Foot Trying to Grow Too Fast

shorts.description:
“Follow your passion” is based on the assumption that you can’t learn to love things.

If you can, then start doing something that makes you money.

And the better you’ll get at it, the more you’ll like it.

Two birds one stone.
shorts.title: You're Using Passion as an Excuse to Avoid Hardness

shorts.description: The hard work of entrepreneurship is the failure that you're inevitably going to encounter by not knowing what you're doing and then taking action steps despite that, with the idea that you will eventually succeed if you don't stop.
shorts.title: You Need Frustration Tolerance

shorts.description:
Everybody is an employee.

You either work for your boss or your customers are your boss.
shorts.title: I Pretended to Be Multiple Employees at My Gym

shorts.description:
When people copy - they copy the wrong stuff because they don’t know why it worked to begin with.

And when it breaks - they don’t know how to fix it because they didn’t build it.

So don’t sweat it. 

Copy cats will always be behind.
shorts.title: Why Copying Makes You A Coward

shorts.description:
I was talking to a friend of mine who decided recently to get into the content game.

He asked why my content was getting more reach than his.

I said “I don’t know. We put out about 250 per week. How many pieces a week are you putting out?”

He replied “I’m posting a measly once a day. Ha! Thank you for resetting my minimum standard.”

He’s already an incredibly successful man (more than me) and it instantly clicked for him. 

Volume. (But there’s more to it than that)

I’ve had this happen to me in business more times than I can count.

I think “oh I should just do 30% more or 50% more.”

But the people who are beating me aren’t doing 50 PERCENT more, they’re doing 50 TIMES more. Big. Difference.

We think we’re doing something wrong, but in reality we aren’t doing nearly enough of it.

To get 5x the results sometimes you have to put in 50x the effort.
shorts.title: You Need to Work 10-30x More Than You Think

shorts.description:
Business is a simple process of expanding the difference between what it costs you to get a customer and how much profit that customer generates over a lifetime.

The bigger the difference the better.
shorts.title: You're Spending $50 to Make $10 in Profit

shorts.description:
The best to place learn marketing for a specific platform from are agency owners.

They walk the walk. Rather than pay for outdated trainings, pay them more than their normal fee to teach you while they execute.

You get the speed of agency and long term benefits of coaching.
shorts.title: Pay the Expert to Teach You, Not to Do the Work

shorts.description:
When selling, boil the sale down to one decision. 

The call agenda isn’t “to see if you’re a good fit for our program/service”

It’s “to decide whether you’d make more money working together than on your own.” Etc.

Clarify to ONE decision. And the moment they say yes, close.
shorts.title: Name Your Cheapest Package 'The Minimum Package'

shorts.description:
If you don’t hear anything good about a new hire in the first 30 days, they’re not good enough.

Excellence makes itself known.
shorts.title: You Can Tell In The First Week If They're A Leader

shorts.description:
I’ve noticed a lot of business lessons I need to relearn at each level. 

How I started:

Focus on one thing
Hire smart people
Think long term

Each of these lessons I’ve had to relearn as companies scaled because:

Focus is even harder when opportunities grow like weeds. They must be trimmed.

What you think smart looks like at $100k per year is very different from what smart looks like at $100M per year.

What feels like long term thinking when you start out is a quarter and eventually becomes multiple years (or decades).

Some lessons are like wine - they age and develop with time.
shorts.title: The Best Talent Is Always in the Future

shorts.description:
Fastest way to increase how smart everyone thinks you are when you walk into a room:

Be the most prepared.

You win the war with the work you do before you sit down to the table, not with what you say after.
shorts.title: Take 5 Minutes Before Every Meeting (and Win Immediately)

shorts.description:
A lot of young leaders think that the point of their job is to keep everyone on their team happy, when in fact, it’s to keep the best people on their team happy.

And allow the rest to rise to the occasion or weed themselves out.

Yes - that means low performers will whine.
It also doesn’t matter.
shorts.title: “Why Can’t I Find Good Leaders?”

shorts.description:
A big reason many don’t make big money later is they spend too much money now.

So when big opportunities come, they can’t take a big swing, because their house, car, and lifestyle costs too much.

If you want to go offensive with money later, you gotta be defensive with it now.
shorts.title: Spend 100% of Your Check and You'll Miss Every Big Opportunity

shorts.description:
How to use downsells:

Only allow them to be sold to unqualified leads. Otherwise, you'll just have a lot of qualified leads buying your downsell instead of your main thing.

And that's because salespeople like closing more than making more money.
shorts.title: Give the Best Closers the Best Leads

shorts.description: The hardest (bootstrapped) revenue level is $1m to $3m in revenue. Main reason: assuming 25% margins, you have $250k to $750k in profit. Typically you need higher value teammates to scale. And they cost...$250k-$750k. So you have to bet everything on an unsure thing. 3 Alternatives: 1) Narrow avatar to more valuable customers, so you can make more money with same infra. 2) Make a better offer you can charge more money for 3) Raise prices. But no matter which path you choose, it takes more risk to get out of "the swamp' than it take to get into it (which is why most get in, and never break out).
shorts.title: I Woke Up With $0 and Wanted to Be a Millionaire. Here's What I'd Do

shorts.description:
Wanna know a what I’ve noticed about the people who own the most profitable businesses?

They think only in terms of profit. As in, they don’t care about revenue or other vanity metrics. They just think - what’s the bottom line. 

And they keep it - the bottom line.
shorts.title: Profit Is Not Natural. You Have to Force It.

shorts.description: In an age of AI, the most valuable business insights won’t come from predicting what will change, but what will stay the same.
shorts.title: “WILL AI KILL MY BUSINESS?”

shorts.description:
In sales scripting, many miss a key point in the first five minutes:

Translating a desire into a decision.

Set the stage up front so everyone is clear what a yes and no look like.
shorts.title: “How Do I Double My Sales?”

shorts.description: If profit were as easy to screenshot as revenue, people would make more of it.
shorts.title: Gross Profit vs Net Profit (Explained in 30 Seconds)

shorts.description:
When you nail your offer, it’s an order of magnitude change in a business. 

You can 2x, 10x, even 100x a business with a better offer. 

Sales - although a valuable skill - can only improve a business incrementally.

This is why we focus on the offer before anything else.
shorts.title: What Separates a $10K Offer from a $10M Offer

shorts.description:
Three options for starting a business:

1) Solve a problem better than others (execution risk)

2) Solve a problem no one knew existed (product-market risk)

3) Solve a problem everyone knows about but is hard to solve (technical risk)

Surest money in 1.
Biggest money in 2 & 3.
shorts.title: The 3 Ways to Start a Business (And Which Makes the Most Money)

shorts.description:
Make it easier, make it faster, make it certain.

Only available now, to a handful of select people, before it runs out.

Replace [it] with whatever outcome your prospect desires. 

This is what makes a compelling offer.
shorts.title: Turn a 5/10 Offer Into a 10/10 Offer

shorts.description:
You always have to sacrifice what you want now for what you want most. 

Feed the dream.
shorts.title: “How Do I Stop Being Average?”

shorts.description:
A big reason many don’t make big money later is they spend too much money now.

So when big opportunities come, they can’t take a big swing, because their house, car, and lifestyle costs too much.

If you want to go offensive with money later, you gotta be defensive with it now.
shorts.title: “Should I Fire Them?”

shorts.description:
Biggest cost reduction that took me too long to learn:

Pay A-players 1.5x market rate to get 5x the output of a B-player.
shorts.title: “Is Cheap Talent Costing Me More?”

shorts.description:
One of my early mentors who recently passed away taught me a marketing lesson Ill never forget:

If you want something to be a big deal. 
Make it a big deal.

Simple, but profound.

Not all things are worth making a big deal out of.
And nothing is inherently a big deal to begin w
shorts.title: I Learned This Trick At 23

shorts.description:
Selling is a transference of belief over a bridge of trust.

Therefore you cannot sell unless you believe. And they will not buy unless they believe YOU.
shorts.title: “How Do I Sell Without Pushing?”

shorts.description:
If you grow 10% per quarter, you 6.7x. 

You can do it by:
1) Selling 10% more customers
2) Increasing customer value 10%

Or, some combination of the above.
shorts.title: “Do I Need More Customers?”

shorts.description: The hardest (bootstrapped) revenue level is $1m to $3m in revenue. Main reason: assuming 25% margins, you have $250k to $750k in profit. Typically you need higher value teammates to scale. And they cost...$250k-$750k. So you have to bet everything on an unsure thing. 3 Alternatives: 1) Narrow avatar to more valuable customers, so you can make more money with same infra. 2) Make a better offer you can charge more money for 3) Raise prices. But no matter which path you choose, it takes more risk to get out of "the swamp' than it take to get into it (which is why most get in, and never break out).
shorts.title: SMBs Suck as Customers

shorts.description:
Losing teaches you one thing:

To avoid losing.
shorts.title: Losing Only Teaches One Lesson

shorts.description:
After years of grinding, when things start working is when most people stop working.

When it gets easy is when you go hard.
shorts.title: When Things Get Easy Is When You Go Hard

shorts.description:
I believe the hardest decision in entrepreneurship is knowing when to give up.

The question is whether the lack of desired success is due to impatience, poor execution, or an opportunity not worth pursuing. 

Imo it’s the decision that requires the most discernment in the game.
shorts.title: This Thing Doesn't Have Value. This Thing Does.

shorts.description: A focused fool can accomplish more than a distracted genius.
shorts.title: “Why Am I Still Not Winning?”

shorts.description: Mr Beast's path to $100 Billion and why I think he (and other creators) are (still) underpriced.
shorts.title: MrBeast Showed Me Who Actually Has the Most Clout

shorts.description:
In a room of one hundred $1M+ entrepreneurs, only 4 make it to $10M+. 

Social Media =\= Reality
shorts.title: Top 0.1% in Any Business Makes $10M

shorts.description: If you’re going to do it eventually, you might as well do it now.
shorts.title: If It's Hard Now With No Kids, It's Impossible Later

shorts.description:
Something that took me a while to figure out:

The easier a business is to scale, the harder it is to start.
shorts.title: Every Business Has a Shape — Which One Are You?

shorts.title: You're Posting Once. I Was Posting 60 Times a Day.

shorts.description:
If you have no money, you should have no shame.

Knock.
Call.
Email.
Text. 
DM.
Ask. 

Life-changing doors don’t open themselves.
shorts.title: If You Have No Money, You Have No Shame

shorts.description:
Instead of the S&P 500, most should invest in the S&Me 500.

10x what you make rather than earning 10% on what you’ve made.
shorts.title: Nothing Has a Higher ROI Than Your Ability to Earn

shorts.description: We stay poor until we’ve learned all the lessons poverty has to teach.
shorts.title: How To Stay Poor

shorts.description:
Beginners overvalue thinking and undervalue doing—

—Advanced do the opposite.
shorts.title: How I Cut Training By 90%
